Predicate adjective of the oath clause חַי־אָנִי. The ASV's fixed rendering of that formula is 'As ... live', and the supplied 'As' is what English spends on the adverbial force of this predicate rather than a conjunction supplied for a clause that lacks one (rule 20); the unit is discontinuous around the pronoun's own word (rule 25) and heads on 'live'. The corpus aligns חַי before a 1cs pronoun to 'as live' in six chapters, including EZK.16.48, EZK.20.3 and EZK.20.31. Marking the 'As' 'added' as a supplied subordinator under rule 55 is the competing reading; it was taken earlier in this chapter and is reversed here.

The oath formula אִם־לֹא is rendered by the single word 'surely'. The polarity reversal leaves neither morpheme's own sense in the English, so the phrase is genuinely indivisible (rule 6) rather than a compositional rule 30 fusion like this chapter's לָכֵן, מִשָּׁם and מִמֶּנּוּ; the corpus reads אִם־לֹא → 'surely' as noncompositional in six of seven two-token occurrences, the seventh (1KI.20.25) conceding the analysis in its own note. Source head is the first token as the deterministic display anchor (rule 6); heading on the negative, and keeping the unit 'aligned', are the competing readings.
